title: My game !
author: Hemicyle2027
selftext:
Hi everyone!



I'd like to share Hémicycle, a free political strategy game that runs right in your browser (PC or phone, nothing to install): [https://hemicyle2027.neocities.org/](https://hemicyle2027.neocities.org/)



The pitch: the President has just dissolved the National Assembly. You lead a party, campaign across all 577 constituencies, try to win a majority (or not...), govern with laws, budgets and the infamous "49.3" (a constitutional article that lets the government force a law through without a vote), survive no-confidence motions... and finally run for President.



What's inside:



\- A real map of France with all 577 constituencies and a realistic two-round voting system: qualification thresholds, three-way runoffs, candidates withdrawing to block a rival, tactical alliances...

\- Create your own party: name, color, symbol, slogan, and an ideology on 5 axes (economy, society, authority, Europe, ecology). A short quiz helps you find where you stand.

\- Life in the National Assembly: electing the Speaker, forming a government, debates before every vote, rebel MPs breaking ranks, opposition bills, forced laws and no-confidence motions.

\- Write your own laws once you're elected as an MP: pick the measure and how it's funded, then try to get it passed.

\- TV debates (party leaders, then the presidential runoff) as a mini-game: attack, hit them with numbers, play on emotion or dodge.

\- Random twists: a billionaire offering to fund your campaign, an embarrassing old video resurfacing, a live TV trap asking you the price of a baguette...

\- An animated election night: 8 pm projections, then the map flips department by department.

\- Secret deals between players ("I'll vote for your bill if you vote for mine")... and betrayals that become public.



Game modes:



\- Solo against 1 to 5 AI opponents who campaign, form alliances, vote and propose their own laws

\- Local multiplayer on the same screen, 2 to 6 players

\- Online with friends (invite link) or in public games, with chat. A free account (Google or email) is required, and it keeps your stats and trophies.



5 starting scenarios (Nationalist Wave, United Left, Economic Crisis...), 3 game lengths and 3 difficulty levels. A tutorial guides you through your first game.



Parties and characters are fictional, but the institutions and mechanics are those of France's Fifth Republic.



Note: the game is currently in French only. If there's interest, I'd love to add an English version!



How I made it: this is a personal project I built with the help of Claude Code, Anthropic's AI coding tool. I came up with the game, chose the features, tested everything and asked for fixes, and Claude Code wrote the code. I thought it was important to be upfront about that!



There are probably still bugs and balance issues. I'd really love your feedback: what's missing, what's overpowered, what party did you create?



Have a great campaign!

comments.body:
This game looks pretty cool, just one thing. 

https://i.redd.it/ulwo0c7j5u1i1.png

this feels kinda biased af.. imo not something you want in your game.

replies.author: Hemicyle2027
replies.body: Thanks, that's a fair point! The idea came from France's real "front républicain" tradition, but you're right that the game shouldn't single out two parties. I'm changing it so you can choose to withdraw against any party, and AI parties now block whichever party is furthest from them ideologically. Same rules for everyone. Thanks for the feedback!

comments.author: oniris
comments.body: It's not bad, but the complete incapacity of the government to improve the economy with anything other than austerity policies is TINA's lack of imagination and ideological bias in my opinion.
